# Transformation of Lorentz Generators under Parity and Time-Reversal

## Setup

The Lorentz group generators are the antisymmetric tensor operators $M^{\rho\sigma}$ ($\rho,\sigma = 0,1,2,3$), from which the rotation and boost generators are defined as

$$J_i = \tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon_{ijk}\,M^{jk}, \qquad K_i = M^{0i}.$$

Under a Lorentz transformation $\Lambda$, the adjoint action on the generators is the tensor transformation law

$$\Lambda\, M^{\rho\sigma}\,\Lambda^{-1} \;=\; \Lambda^{\rho}{}_{\alpha}\,\Lambda^{\sigma}{}_{\beta}\,M^{\alpha\beta}\,\sigma_{\mathcal{O}}, \tag{1}$$

where $\sigma_{\mathcal{O}} = +1$ for a **unitary** operation (parity) and $\sigma_{\mathcal{O}} = -1$ for an **anti-unitary** operation (time reversal). The extra sign for time reversal arises because the quantum operators $M^{\rho\sigma}$ carry an explicit factor of $i$ in their definition, and an anti-unitary operator complex-conjugates: $\Theta\,(i)\,\Theta^{-1} = -i$.

The discrete transformations are
$$\Lambda_P = \mathrm{diag}(+1,-1,-1,-1) \quad\text{(parity)},\qquad \Lambda_T = \mathrm{diag}(-1,+1,+1,+1) \quad\text{(time reversal)}.$$

---

## Parity ($\Lambda_P$, unitary, $\sigma = +1$)

**Rotations $J_i = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_{ijk}M^{jk}$.** Both indices of $M^{jk}$ are spatial, so each picks up a factor $(-1)$ from $\Lambda_P$:

$$\Lambda_P\, M^{jk}\,\Lambda_P^{-1} = (-1)(-1)\,M^{jk} = +M^{jk}.$$

Contracting with $\epsilon_{ijk}$:

$$\boxed{\;\Lambda_P\, J_i\,\Lambda_P^{-1} = +J_i\;} \qquad\text{(rotations are even under parity).}$$

**Boosts $K_i = M^{0i}$.** The index $0$ is temporal (factor $+1$) and the index $i$ is spatial (factor $-1$):

$$\Lambda_P\, M^{0i}\,\Lambda_P^{-1} = (+1)(-1)\,M^{0i} = -M^{0i}.$$

$$\boxed{\;\Lambda_P\, K_i\,\Lambda_P^{-1} = -K_i\;} \qquad\text{(boosts are odd under parity).}$$

---

## Time Reversal ($\Lambda_T$, anti-unitary, $\sigma = -1$)

The anti-unitary sign $\sigma = -1$ contributes an overall minus sign on top of the tensor-index factors.

**Rotations $J_i = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_{ijk}M^{jk}$.** Both indices are spatial, each picking up $+1$ from $\Lambda_T$, giving a tensor factor of $(+1)$. Combined with the anti-unitary sign:

$$\Lambda_T\, M^{jk}\,\Lambda_T^{-1} = (+1)(+1)\,(-1)\,M^{jk} = -M^{jk}.$$

$$\boxed{\;\Lambda_T\, J_i\,\Lambda_T^{-1} = -J_i\;} \qquad\text{(rotations are odd under time reversal).}$$

**Boosts $K_i = M^{0i}$.** The index $0$ picks up $(-1)$ and the index $i$ picks up $(+1)$, giving a tensor factor of $(-1)$. Combined with the anti-unitary sign:

$$\Lambda_T\, M^{0i}\,\Lambda_T^{-1} = (-1)(+1)\,(-1)\,M^{0i} = +M^{0i}.$$

$$\boxed{\;\Lambda_T\, K_i\,\Lambda_T^{-1} = +K_i\;} \qquad\text{(boosts are even under time reversal).}$$

---

## Consistency Check: The Algebra Is Preserved

The Lorentz algebra is
$$[J_i,J_j]=i\epsilon_{ijk}J_k,\quad [J_i,K_j]=i\epsilon_{ijk}K_k,\quad [K_i,K_j]=-i\epsilon_{ijk}J_k.$$

**Under parity** ($J_i\to J_i,\;K_i\to -K_i$, $i$ unchanged):
- $[J_i,J_j]\to[J_i,J_j]=i\epsilon_{ijk}J_k$ ✓
- $[J_i,K_j]\to[J_i,-K_j]=-i\epsilon_{ijk}K_k=i\epsilon_{ijk}(-K_k)$ ✓
- $[K_i,K_j]\to[-K_i,-K_j]=[K_i,K_j]=-i\epsilon_{ijk}J_k$ ✓

**Under time reversal** ($J_i\to -J_i,\;K_i\to K_i$, and $i\to -i$ by anti-unitarity):
- $[J_i,J_j]\to[-J_i,-J_j]=[J_i,J_j]$; RHS: $(-i)\epsilon_{ijk}(-J_k)=i\epsilon_{ijk}J_k$ ✓
- $[J_i,K_j]\to[-J_i,K_j]=-[J_i,K_j]=-i\epsilon_{ijk}K_k$; RHS: $(-i)\epsilon_{ijk}K_k=-i\epsilon_{ijk}K_k$ ✓
- $[K_i,K_j]\to[K_i,K_j]=-i\epsilon_{ijk}J_k$; RHS: $-(-i)\epsilon_{ijk}(-J_k)=-i\epsilon_{ijk}J_k$ ✓

All three commutation relations are preserved in both cases.

---

## Physical Interpretation

The result can be understood through the relativistic angular-momentum tensor $M^{\mu\nu}=x^\mu p^\nu - x^\nu p^\mu$, so $K_i = M^{0i} = t\,p_i - x_i\,E$:

- **$J_i \sim \mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{p}$ (angular momentum, a pseudovector):** Under parity $\mathbf{r}\to-\mathbf{r},\,\mathbf{p}\to-\mathbf{p}$, so $\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{p}\to(+)\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{p}$ (even). Under time reversal $\mathbf{p}\to-\mathbf{p},\,\mathbf{r}\to\mathbf{r}$, so $\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{p}\to(-)\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{p}$ (odd).
- **$K_i \sim t\,p_i - x_i\,E$ (boost generator):** Under parity $t\to t,\,p_i\to-p_i,\,x_i\to-x_i,\,E\to E$, giving $t(-p_i)-(-x_i)E = -(tp_i-x_iE)$ (odd). Under time reversal $t\to-t,\,p_i\to-p_i,\,x_i\to x_i,\,E\to E$, giving $(-t)(-p_i)-x_iE = tp_i-x_iE$ (even).

This matches the algebraic derivation exactly.

---

## Summary

| Generator | Parity $\Lambda_P$ (unitary) | Time reversal $\Lambda_T$ (anti-unitary) |
|-----------|------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| $J_i$ (rotation) | $+J_i$ (even) | $-J_i$ (odd) |
| $K_i$ (boost) | $-K_i$ (odd) | $+K_i$ (even) |

The key distinction between the two discrete symmetries is that parity is unitary (only tensor-index signs matter) while time reversal is anti-unitary (an additional overall minus sign from $i\to -i$ flips the parity of each generator's transformation. This is why rotations, even under parity, become odd under time reversal, and boosts, odd under parity, become even under time reversal.

$$J_i = \tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon_{ijk}\,M^{jk}, \qquad K_i = M^{0i}.$$

$$\Lambda\, M^{\rho\sigma}\,\Lambda^{-1} \;=\; \Lambda^{\rho}{}_{\alpha}\,\Lambda^{\sigma}{}_{\beta}\,M^{\alpha\beta}\,\sigma_{\mathcal{O}}, \tag{1}$$

The extra sign for time reversal arises because the quantum operators $M^{\rho\sigma}$ carry an explicit factor of $i$ in their definition, and an anti-unitary operator complex-conjugates: $\Theta\,(i)\,\Theta^{-1} = -i$.

The discrete transformations are
$$\Lambda_P = \mathrm{diag}(+1,-1,-1,-1) \quad\text{(parity)},\qquad \Lambda_T = \mathrm{diag}(-1,+1,+1,+1) \quad\text{(time reversal)}.$$

---

## Parity ($\Lambda_P$, unitary, $\sigma = +1$)

**Rotations $J_i = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_{ijk}M^{jk}$.** Both indices of $M^{jk}$ are spatial, so each picks up a factor $(-1)$ from $\Lambda_P$:

Contracting with $\epsilon_{ijk}$:

**Boosts $K_i = M^{0i}$.** The index $0$ is temporal (factor $+1$) and the index $i$ is spatial (factor $-1$):

$$\Lambda_P\, M^{0i}\,\Lambda_P^{-1} = (+1)(-1)\,M^{0i} = -M^{0i}.$$

$$\boxed{\;\Lambda_P\, K_i\,\Lambda_P^{-1} = -K_i\;} \qquad\text{(boosts are odd under parity).}$$

---

## Time Reversal ($\Lambda_T$, anti-unitary, $\sigma = -1$)

The anti-unitary sign $\sigma = -1$ contributes an overall minus sign on top of the tensor-index factors.

**Rotations $J_i = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_{ijk}M^{jk}$.** Both indices are spatial, each picking up $+1$ from $\Lambda_T$, giving a tensor factor of $(+1)$. Combined with the anti-unitary sign:

$$\Lambda_T\, M^{jk}\,\Lambda_T^{-1} = (+1)(+1)\,(-1)\,M^{jk} = -M^{jk}.$$

$$\boxed{\;\Lambda_T\, J_i\,\Lambda_T^{-1} = -J_i\;} \qquad\text{(rotations are odd under time reversal).}$$

**Boosts $K_i = M^{0i}$.** The index $0$ picks up $(-1)$ and the index $i$ picks up $(+1)$, giving a tensor factor of $(-1)$. Combined with the anti-unitary sign:

$$\Lambda_T\, M^{0i}\,\Lambda_T^{-1} = (-1)(+1)\,(-1)\,M^{0i} = +M^{0i}.$$

$$\boxed{\;\Lambda_T\, K_i\,\Lambda_T^{-1} = +K_i\;} \qquad\text{(boosts are even under time reversal).}$$

The Lorentz algebra is
$$[J_i,J_j]=i\epsilon_{ijk}J_k,\quad [J_i,K_j]=i\epsilon_{ijk}K_k,\quad [K_i,K_j]=-i\epsilon_{ijk}J_k.$$

**Under time reversal** ($J_i\to -J_i,\;K_i\to K_i$, and $i\to -i$ by anti-unitarity):
- $[J_i,J_j]\to[-J_i,-J_j]=[J_i,J_j]$; RHS: $(-i)\epsilon_{ijk}(-J_k)=i\epsilon_{ijk}J_k$ ✓

Under time reversal $\mathbf{p}\to-\mathbf{p},\,\mathbf{r}\to\mathbf{r}$, so $\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{p}\to(-)\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{p}$ (odd).

This matches the algebraic derivation exactly.

---

|-----------|------------------------------|------------------------------------------|

| $K_i$ (boost) | $-K_i$ (odd) | $+K_i$ (even) |
